What

What Lot Clearing Involves

Lot clearing is full-scope vegetation removal across an entire parcel or a defined portion of it — standing trees, brush and undergrowth, and the root systems underneath. Instead of hiring a tree crew, a stump grinder, and a grading contractor separately, Roubic folds tree removal, brush removal, stump grinding, and final grading into a single coordinated contract with one written line-item quote.

The jobs that matter most here are the rural-suburban parcels common across Geauga County — Auburn Township, Bainbridge Township, and Chesterland — where 1 to 10+ acre lots get cleared for new-home construction, a residential addition, a driveway corridor, or pasture use. Every lot-clearing contract starts with an on-site scope walk so the acreage, tree count, density, and stump count are priced before any equipment rolls in.

Common Lot Clearing Questions

Lot Clearing FAQ

Five things NE Ohio property owners want to know before booking.

How much does lot clearing cost?
Lot clearing pricing is scope-specific. Most residential lot-clearing jobs run $1,500–$15,000 depending on acreage, density, tree count, and stump count. Large rural parcels can exceed $25,000. Coordinated clearing + stumping + final grade is typically 10–20% cheaper than booking three subcontractors separately, and every parcel gets a written line-item quote.
Do I need a permit for lot clearing?
Maybe. Large-scale clearing that changes land use can trigger zoning review, and requirements depend on parcel size, scope, and whether protected canopy is involved. Roubic confirms permit requirements as part of every estimate before any work begins.
Can Roubic clear a lot for new home construction?
Yes — full-lot clearing for new construction is core Roubic work. We typically coordinate with the homeowner's general contractor and align our schedule with the foundation-pour timing so the site is ready when the build starts.
How long does lot clearing take?
A typical 1-acre clearing job runs 2–4 days. A 5-acre job runs 1–2 weeks. The schedule depends on tree density, stump count, weather, and final-grade complexity — Aaron confirms the timeline during the free scope walk.
Does lot clearing include stump removal and final grading?
Yes. A full lot-clearing contract combines tree removal, brush and undergrowth removal, stump grinding or excavation (depending on planned land use), and final grading to spec — with optional rough seeding for erosion control. It's all handled under one coordinated contract rather than separate bookings.
